Description
	 
		(last modified by Guillermo Bonvehí)
	 
I'm sporadically getting some cache errors using database backend.
The error is: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
And the backtrace:
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/core/handlers/base.py:143→ _get_response
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/template/response.py:108→ render
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/utils/decorators.py:156→ callback
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/middleware/cache.py:103→ process_response
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/utils/cache.py:374→ learn_cache_key
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/core/cache/backends/db.py:104→ set
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/core/cache/backends/db.py:136→ _base_set
/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/django/core/cache/backends/db.py:277→ _cull
This is using Django 2.2.11 but I see the same code is in master.
​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/core/cache/backends/db.py#L270
				cursor.execute(
					connection.ops.cache_key_culling_sql() % table,
					[cull_num])
				cursor.execute("DELETE FROM %s "
							 "WHERE cache_key < %%s" % table,
							 [cursor.fetchone()[0]])
From what I can understand, the cursor after running connection.ops.cache_key_culling_sql() command is not returning any data, so cursor.fetchone()[0] afterwards fails.
I guess a simple check to see if it contains data would be enough, may apply for an easy picking.

Now I understand the issue. The `cache_key_culling_sql()` returns a SELECT query that retrieves the first cache key greater than the n smallest. When executed with an offset equal to `cull_num`, it may return no rows if there aren't enough rows in the table.

This can happen due to race conditions:
1. Thread A checks `num > self._max_entries` and it's True
2. Thread B also deletes some cache entries
3. When Thread A runs the culling SQL query, there may not be enough rows anymore

The change looks correct. The fix:

1. Stores the result of `cursor.fetchone()` in a variable `last_cache_key`
2. Checks if `last_cache_key` is not None before trying to access `last_cache_key[0]`
3. Only executes the DELETE statement if there's actually a key to delete

This handles the race condition gracefully - if between the COUNT and the SELECT queries some other process deletes entries from the cache, and there are no more rows to fetch, we simply don't execute the DELETE (because there's nothing to delete anyway).
